auth.nameHint: How people and agents see you.

auth.setupPasswordHint: The value of PLAINBOARD_PASSWORD in the .env file next to your docker-compose.yml. It is asked once, so nobody else can claim a new server.
auth.setupOpen: This installation has no setup password
auth.setupOpenHint: Whoever opens this address first becomes its admin. If others can reach it, stop here: write PLAINBOARD_PASSWORD=your-own-password into the .env file next to your docker-compose.yml, run docker compose up -d and open this page again.

browser.openTab: Open in a tab of your own browser
browser.closed: The connection to the browser ended.
browser.emptyTitle: A browser next to your agents
browser.emptyHint: Pages of a server an agent started run here as they do at localhost, so apps work that break as a preview link. Servers that run are listed here. You can also enter an address like localhost:5173.
browser.startHint: A page opened here runs at localhost, as the app expects. In a new tab it is faster, but some apps break behind the preview link.

chat.label: Chat
chat.showCodeHint: With the eye on, edits, new files and commands appear as lines that open to the code. Only for you, in this browser.

design.label: Design
design.fahrplanHint: Ruled rows and one type size, like a timetable.
design.classicHint: Cards, rounded corners and an indigo accent.
design.slop2getherHint: Like slop2gether.com: near-black stage, big radii, pill buttons, orange.

status.noCredentials: No subscription yet: add one in the PlainBoard settings

update.how_one: A newer PlainBoard is available ({{count}} commit ahead). On the server: docker compose pull, then docker compose up -d (built from a clone: git pull, then docker compose up -d --build).
update.how_other: A newer PlainBoard is available ({{count}} commits ahead). On the server: docker compose pull, then docker compose up -d (built from a clone: git pull, then docker compose up -d --build).

toolset.board: Coordinator: plans and hands out work
toolset.fullHint: Has a shell, files, git and the web, and the board.
toolset.boardHint: Has the board, and a shell for small things. Its prompt is much shorter, so it uses less of the quota.

projects.noneHint: A project has its own board, team of agents, notes and schedules.
projects.name: Name
projects.languageHint: What the agents write to you in: in the chat, in questions and in tickets. Empty: the language each person writes in. Code and commits are not affected.
projects.descriptionHint: What is being built, for whom, and what matters. Part of every agent's briefing, so keep it short. The manager writes it after talking with you; change it here whenever you like.
projects.localFolderHint: Normally every agent works in its own copy of the code. Name a folder inside the workspaces directory here to have all agents work in the same one instead, for example a project folder of your own machine that is mounted there. Repositories are cloned into sub folders of it.
projects.publicApiHint: Lets a website load tickets that have a customer title, with their customer texts and nothing else. Create one key per place that uses it, so you can revoke one without breaking the others. Add ?lang=de to get the texts in one of the customer languages; a ticket without them there comes in the default language, and each ticket says which one it is in (lang).
projects.publicApiCopy: Copy this key now, it is only shown once:
projects.githubTokenHint: Only if this project needs another GitHub account than the one in the PlainBoard settings. Empty: that one is used.
projects.githubTokenSet: A project token is stored. Enter a new one to replace it.
projects.autoWake: Tell the manager when work is finished
projects.fastChecksHint: PlainBoard measures every check run. Once for each repository, and again when its checks get clearly slower than they were (or than a target you set), the manager has them made faster: caching, parallel jobs, no double work. Nothing is checked less. Switched off, PlainBoard leaves the checks as they are.
projects.semanticSearchHint: The agents can search this project's history by meaning, in any language: earlier tickets, reports, decisions, comments, notes and commits. They search when work may have history, not on every turn. Switched off, nothing of this project is indexed and the agents have no search.
projects.autoWakeHint: The manager gets the reports of finished work by itself and goes on from there. Switched off, it looks at them only when you write to it.
projects.backlogNext: Go on with the Backlog when To Do cannot start
projects.backlogNextHint: When nothing in To Do can start, the team takes the next Backlog tickets, the most urgent first, and leaves only what needs you. Switched off, the Backlog waits until you move a ticket to To Do, and the team rests when To Do is empty.
projects.repositoriesHint: Every agent gets its own copy of each repository; in the team you choose which agent gets which.
projects.repoCheckHint: Decides whether work may stay: your test suite or CI script. Runs once for all finished branches together, with any git host. Empty: on GitHub, the checks of a pull request decide.
projects.repoLandFirstHint: A finished branch is merged at once, after the quick check. The full check runs on the base branch afterwards, once for everything that arrived; if it fails, an agent repairs it, and until then (at most 45 minutes) only that repair is merged. Much faster where checks take long or often fail, but the base branch can be broken for a while: right for a development branch, not for one you release from.
projects.repoQuickCheckHint: Runs the moment an agent hands over a branch: formatting, lint, whatever takes a minute or two. A failure goes straight back to that agent instead of costing everyone a full check. Empty: none.
projects.confirmRemoveRepo: Remove repository "{{name}}" from the project? Existing clones stay on disk.
projects.githubNoToken: To choose from GitHub, add a GitHub token: PlainBoard settings → Code access, or Project settings → Advanced. Without one, add the repository by its address.
projects.autoArchiveHint: Archived tickets leave the board and keep their history and links. 0: never.
projects.retention: Delete the files of done tickets
projects.retentionHint: Off by default: no file is ever deleted. When on, a daily run deletes the files of tickets in the status done for this many days, counted from when they were set to done; a ticket opened again starts over when it is done again. Only the status counts: tickets in any other status are never touched, archived or not, nor files still used in an open question, a chat, a note, an idea or an open ticket. The entry stays on the ticket with name and size, and the manager is told what went.
projects.retentionNow: Deleted at the next daily run: {{count}} files ({{size}}).
projects.retentionSoon: Within the following {{days}} days: {{count}} more files ({{size}}).
projects.retentionKept: The entries stay on the tickets with name and size. Deleted files cannot be restored.
projects.parallel: Agents working at the same time
projects.pauseHint: Nothing of this project starts while it is paused: no turn, no schedule, no landing, whoever asks. Turns that run wrap up, background jobs are stopped, messages wait. It stays paused across restarts and when "Pause everything" ends, until someone resumes it here.
projects.pausedBanner: This project is paused by {{by}}. Nothing of it starts, and messages wait, until it is resumed.
projects.parallelHint: How many members of this project work at once. Empty: the number from the PlainBoard settings ({{count}}). 0 pauses them; the manager still answers.
projects.reviewDays: Finish tickets left in review after (days)
projects.reviewDaysHint: A ticket in review that nobody touched for this long moves to done by itself. Tickets with a question or a task for you stay. 0: never.
projects.repoAccessDefault: The general access from the PlainBoard settings
projects.repoAccessToken: A token only for this repository
projects.repoAccessSsh: An SSH key only for this repository (deploy key)
projects.repoAccessDefaultHint: HTTPS addresses use the GitHub token from the PlainBoard settings or from this project; SSH addresses use the SSH key from the PlainBoard settings. Public repositories that are only read need neither.
projects.repoAccessTokenHint: A token for this repository alone, from any git host over HTTPS: GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Bitbucket.
projects.repoTokenStored: Stored. Enter a new one to replace it.
projects.repoTokenUser: User name (only if the host needs one)
projects.repoAccessSshHint: Works with every git host and needs no account token. Agents can clone and push; opening pull requests still takes a token.
projects.repoSshOnSave: PlainBoard creates a key pair when you save and shows the public key in the list (key button). The address is changed to its SSH form.
projects.repoSshPublicKeyHint: Add it at your git host. GitHub: repository → Settings → Deploy keys → Add deploy key, with write access. GitLab: Settings → Repository → Deploy keys.
projects.repoSshCopyKey: Copy the public key (add it at your git host as a deploy key)
projects.repoSshNew: Create a new key on save
projects.repoSshOwn: Or use your own private key
projects.publicApiLabel: Label, e.g. Website or Status page
projects.publicApiConfirmRevoke: Revoke the key "{{name}}"? Whatever uses it stops working.
projects.noneSharedHint: No project has been shared with you yet. Ask an owner or an admin to add you.
projects.repoUrlHint: The address you would clone it from, HTTPS or SSH.
projects.repoBranchHint: Where finished work ends up. Empty: the repository's default branch.
projects.repoNameHint: The folder agents find it in. Empty: taken from the address.
projects.repoDescriptionHint: One line. Helps the manager give the right work to the right agent.
projects.repoTidy: Remove branches that are fully on the base branch
projects.repoTidyHint: Every hour and after each landing, PlainBoard deletes the branches whose content is all on the base branch already, also when they were squashed, rebased or landed inside another branch. Anything not proven to be there stays, and so do the base and default branch, protected branches, branches of open pull requests, what PlainBoard has in flight, and anything with a commit younger than an hour. The manager is told each deleted branch with its commit, so it can be restored; old branches with unmerged work are only named to it.
projects.repoLandingHint: An agent hands over its finished branch and goes on with other work. PlainBoard brings the branches to the base branch by itself.
projects.repoLandWhen: When does a finished branch reach the base branch?
projects.repoLandCheckedHint: PlainBoard merges all finished branches, checks them once together, and only what passes reaches the base branch. Right for a branch you release from, and where checks are quick and reliable.
projects.repoCheckTarget: Target duration of a check run (minutes)
projects.repoCheckTargetHint: Optional. With Keep checks fast on, a check run over it has the team make the checks faster. Empty: no target, only clear growth counts.
projects.newGithub: Or create a new repository on GitHub
projects.newGithubHint: Created with the GitHub token, with a first commit, and added to this project. A classic token needs the scope repo, a fine-grained one the permission "Administration: write".
projects.newGithubFailed: GitHub did not create the repository.
projects.githubMissingHint: The list shows what your GitHub token can reach: your own repositories, those you collaborate on and those of your organisations. A classic token needs the repo scope, and where an organisation uses single sign-on it must be authorised for that organisation. A fine-grained token only reaches the one account or organisation it was created for, so an organisation needs a token of its own (as the project's GitHub token: Project settings, Advanced). Any repository can also be added by its address.
projects.askModelHint: What answers questions asked with Ctrl+Enter in the chat. It only reads, so a small model is usually enough. Empty: Claude Haiku with effort high.
projects.ideaModelHint: What reads, sorts and rearranges the ideas of this project. A small model is enough. Empty: the provider's small model.

board.hint: Move a ticket to In Progress (or open it and click “Hand to manager”) to let the manager plan and delegate it.
board.newTicketKeys: Enter to add · Ctrl+Enter to add and open · Esc to cancel
board.managerPlanning: Manager is working on this ticket

landing.waiting: Finished: the branch waits to land
landing.checking: Finished: the branch is being checked before it lands
landing.repairing: Finished: the branch is being repaired before it lands

stats.title: Statistics
stats.subtitle: What happened in this project. Days are in UTC.
stats.reportHint: A file with where turns, time and cost went, per agent and ticket. Numbers and tool names only, no texts.
stats.logHint: Everything of this period as it happened: every turn with its prompt and answer, every tool call with input and result, assignments, updates, jobs and landing. It contains your project's texts and code, but no passwords or tokens: give it only to someone you would show the project.
stats.cycleHint: Median, from starting work to done
stats.slowdownsHint: Found by PlainBoard's own checks in the last 24 hours, heaviest first. The manager sees the same list and acts on it in its daily tidy-up; you can also ask it to.
stats.slowdownsNone: PlainBoard's own checks found nothing in the last 24 hours.
stats.speedHint: How fast finished work reaches the base branch and what that costs, against the same number of days before.
stats.updateMarks: A dashed line marks a day on which PlainBoard itself was updated.
stats.noAgents: No agent has worked in this period.

ticket.customerHint: Public on your website, in simple words. Without a title, customers don't see this ticket.
ticket.customerMissingTab: Not written in this language yet
ticket.customerDefaultHint: Default language: without a title here, customers don't see this ticket in any language.
ticket.handToManagerHint: The manager splits the ticket into clear assignments for the right agents.
ticket.descriptionPlaceholder: What should be done? Markdown supported. Paste images to attach them.
ticket.dropFiles: Drop files here or paste images
ticket.stateHint: Kept by PlainBoard from the reports of the assignments: what is done, open, decided, and what was tried and dropped. Agents get it with every assignment on this ticket, so nothing is done twice.

decision.title: Your decision
decision.notePlaceholder: Add a note to your choice, or answer in your own words…

lightbox.zoomIn: Zoom in (+, or the mouse wheel)

chat.copying: {{name}} is working… Copying attachments to the runner: {{done}} of {{total}}
chat.readWaiting: {{name}} has read this and answers next

limits.unknown: No usage known yet. It appears after the next agent turn at the latest.
limits.noPlan: You are signed in with an API key, which has no plan limits. Add a subscription under PlainBoard settings → Subscriptions to see them here.

chat.compressHint: Summarize older messages with the summary model.
chat.resetHint: Keeps memory and recent messages, drops the provider session.
chat.contextTitle: Context: {{used}} of {{limit}} tokens (fixed base ~{{base}}). Compression starts above the limit.
chat.introManager: Describe what you want to build. The manager creates tickets, builds the team, delegates work and keeps you posted.
chat.introAgent: Talk to this agent directly. It answers from its own context.
chat.compactedByProvider: Context compacted by the provider during the run ({{tokens}} tokens before)
chat.freshContext: New context for the next piece of work ({{tokens}} tokens left behind)

starters.hint: Not sure how to begin? Start from one of these and fill in the rest:

build.label: Build something new
build.text:
I want to build: 

It should: 

Plan it as tickets first and ask me whatever is unclear before anyone starts.

existing.label: Work on code that exists
existing.text: Look at the repository and tell me in a few lines what it is and how it is built. Then propose the team you would set up for it. Change nothing yet.

change.label: Change or fix one thing
change.text:
Please change: 

Tell me when it is done and how I can check it.

ask.title: Quick question
ask.button: Send as a quick question ({{shortcut}}): a fast agent answers only you
ask.private: Only you see this. A fast agent looks it up in the code, tickets and history; it changes nothing, and the manager neither waits for it nor learns of it.
ask.broken: The answer broke off. Ask again.

todos.title: Tasks of {{name}}
todos.doneHint: Done tasks move to the archive after 7 days and are deleted after 90 days. Agents only see open tasks.

ownNotes.title: Notes of {{name}}
ownNotes.hint: What this member must not forget. These notes are always part of its prompt, also after its context is reset or compressed. The member adds notes itself, and you can add, change and delete them here.

team.title: Team
team.subtitle: Each agent has one area of its own, so it stays quick and cheap. The manager builds and changes the team too.
team.contextTitle: Current context / compression limit · total cost
team.name: Name
team.areaHint: The part of the project that is this agent's. The manager decides by it who gets which work.
team.instructionsHint: Anything this agent should always do or never do. It reads them on every turn, so keep them short.
team.accountHint: Automatic: the project's subscription, else the one with the most room left. API keys only when every subscription is used up.
team.defaultModel: The one from the PlainBoard settings
team.effortHint: How long it thinks before it acts. Lower is faster and uses less of the quota.
team.contextLimitHint: Beyond this, older messages are replaced by a summary. Every turn reads the whole chat again, so a smaller number makes each turn cheaper and faster.
team.summaryModelHint: Routine work: the small model is enough. Below it, how long it thinks about a summary.
team.summaryEffortDefault: Effort: as in the PlainBoard settings ({{effort}})
team.keepRecent: Latest messages kept as they are
team.keepRecentHint: They stay word for word when the chat is summarised.
team.mcpServersHint: Tools from the Tools view that are not given to every agent.
team.baseContext: Fixed base context of this agent: ~{{tokens}} tokens (system prompt, tools, memory). Compression starts once the conversation grows at least 4k beyond it.
team.repositoriesHint: It gets its own copy of these and knows nothing of the others.
team.allRepos: All repositories, also ones added later
team.modelHint: Stronger models decide better and cost more of the quota.
team.enabledHint: Switched off, the agent starts nothing new. It keeps its work and goes on with it when you switch it on again.
team.advancedHint: The values from the PlainBoard settings fit most agents. Change these only for a reason.
team.providerHint: Which kind of AI this agent is. It decides which models and subscriptions it can use.

notes.title: Notes
notes.hint: Durable project knowledge for you and the agents. Pinned notes are part of every agent's prompt.
notes.pinnedHint: Always in every agent's context (costs tokens).
notes.budgetHint: Characters of pinned notes added to every agent's prompt. Beyond the budget only titles are included.

schedules.title: Schedules
schedules.subtitle: Run a prompt for an agent at a given time or on a recurring schedule.
schedules.emptyHint: Examples: a daily status report, a weekly dependency check, a reminder.
schedules.name: Name
schedules.promptHint: What the agent should do when the schedule fires.
schedules.cronHint: minute hour day month weekday, e.g. 0 9 * * 1-5
schedules.skipQuiet: Leave out a run when nothing happened since the last one
schedules.skipQuietHint: For status reports: no turn is spent on "nothing new". What counts: an agent's turn, a ticket moved, a branch landed. Leave it off for a schedule that looks at something outside the project.

tools.title: Tools
tools.subtitle: Connect MCP servers to give agents extra tools. stdio servers run inside the runner container.
tools.emptyHint: Agents already have shell, git, GitHub CLI and the board. Add MCP servers for anything else.
tools.name: Name
tools.commandHint: e.g. npx, uvx or an absolute path
tools.selectAgentsHint: Pick the agents in the agent editor (Team).

accounts.label: Account name
accounts.confirmDelete: Delete account "{{name}}"? A ChatGPT sign-in on the runner is signed out.
accounts.rotationHint: A conversation stays on its subscription while its prompt cache is warm, until that reaches 95 % or hits a limit. New conversations, and those idle for an hour or starting a fresh context, go to the subscription with the most usage left, counted by the size of its plan. The last 5 % of every subscription are used once all are that full, API keys only after that. A project or an agent can be given one of its own: Project settings → Team, or the agent in Team.
accounts.planSizeHint: How much usage the plan allows, as a multiple of the smallest plan (Claude Pro = 1, Max 5x = 5, Max 20x = 20). Empty: as detected, otherwise like the other subscriptions.
accounts.noneOwn: Nobody has added a subscription of their own.

share.label: Who may use it
share.nobody: Nobody else has an account here yet.
share.hint: Their projects may run on it. They see its name and how much is used, never its token or key.

projectAccounts.label: Subscriptions this project may use
projectAccounts.hint: Nothing ticked: any of the installation's. Tick some, and this project's agents run on those only, whatever anyone chooses for an agent. For a project you share with others, when another subscription is meant for your own work.
projectAccounts.readonly: This project may only use: {{names}}. An admin decides that.

givenAccounts.label: Own subscriptions
givenAccounts.description: Whoever works in this project can give it their own subscriptions, without its owner.
givenAccounts.mineHint: Its runs in this project may use it, also if it is set to “Only me”. Who may use it in their own projects is still what “Who may use it” says. Nobody here sees its token or key. Take it back at any time: a turn on it finishes, the next one takes another subscription.
givenAccounts.noneMine: You have no subscription of your own. Add one in PlainBoard settings, My subscriptions.
givenAccounts.blockedMine: The project's owner switched it off for this project.
givenAccounts.noneOthers: No member has given this project a subscription.
givenAccounts.unused: not in use: its owner no longer works in this project
givenAccounts.ownerHint: Switch one off and this project's runs no longer use it. You never see its token or key.
givenAccounts.toProjectsHint: The runs of the projects ticked here may use it, also if it is set to “Only me”. Each project's owner sees its name and yours, never its token or key, and can switch it off for their project.

endpoints.title: Other models
endpoints.hint: Models of your own or of other hosts: a model server on your machine or in your network (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM), Gemini, or a host or gateway that speaks one of the two common interfaces. An agent on such a model works with the same tools as one on Claude. How well it does depends on the model: it has to call tools reliably and read a long prompt.
endpoints.confirmDelete: Delete "{{name}}"? Agents that run on its models have no account for them then.
endpoints.addressHint: Empty: {{url}}. From inside PlainBoard's containers your own machine is host.docker.internal, not localhost.
endpoints.addressNeeded: Where the server answers, e.g. https://host/v1. From inside PlainBoard's containers your own machine is host.docker.internal, not localhost.
endpoints.keyOptional: API key (only if the server asks for one)
endpoints.keyNotNeeded: Not set, and usually not needed
endpoints.modelsHint: One per line, named as the server names them.
endpoints.modelsHintUsual: One per line, named as the server names them. Empty: the usual ones, shown in grey.
endpoints.contextHint: How much these models take at once. The agent sums up its work before it gets there. Empty: 128,000. Too high, and the server refuses a long turn; a model server of your own often has far less until you raise it.
endpoints.loadEmpty: The server named no models. Type them in above.

settings.memberChatHint: Off: you talk to the manager, and members' conversations can only be read. Agents still talk to each other, and schedules and assignments are not affected.
settings.updateCheck: Tell me when a newer PlainBoard is available
settings.updateCheckHint: Every few hours PlainBoard asks GitHub whether its repository has newer commits than the one that is running. Only that commit id is sent.
settings.databaseSqlite: Database: SQLite, one file in the data volume.
settings.databaseMoveHint: Move it to PostgreSQL, with all data: PlainBoard restarts, copies every table and counts the rows, and serves again after a few minutes.
settings.databaseConfirm:
Move to PostgreSQL now?

PlainBoard restarts and is away for a few minutes while every table is copied and counted. The SQLite file stays in the data volume as a backup; if anything fails, PlainBoard goes on with SQLite.

Back up the data volume first, and pause the agents if they are working.
settings.databaseRestarting: PlainBoard restarts and moves the data now; this page is back when it serves again. If it does not come back by itself, run docker compose up -d.
settings.databaseFailed: The last move to PostgreSQL failed, nothing changed: {{reason}}
settings.databaseNotEmpty: The bundled PostgreSQL database holds data already, so nothing is moved into it.
settings.databaseMoveSteps: To move to PostgreSQL, with all data: take the current docker-compose.yml, run docker compose up -d, and come back here.
settings.title: PlainBoard settings
settings.claudeHint: Subscriptions and API keys for agents that run on Claude.

auth.runner_loginHint: Sign in with the Claude account

settings.codexHint: Subscriptions and API keys for agents that run on OpenAI models with Codex. Which one an agent uses is chosen per agent.

codexAuth.chatgptHint: Sign in with your ChatGPT plan

settings.codexDeviceCode: Open this page, sign in with your ChatGPT account and enter the code:
settings.claudeOpenPage: Open this page and sign in with your Claude account. The page then shows a code: copy all of it and enter it here.
settings.codexOwnLoginNotice: Uses your own ChatGPT account. Whether this is allowed for third-party tools depends on OpenAI's terms for your plan.
settings.readAccessHint: A key with which a tool or a person can read everything here and change nothing: chats, tickets, runs, the full log and the database. Passwords and tokens stay hidden. It is sent as "Authorization: Bearer <key>" to the API. Revoke a key and it stops working at once.
settings.readAccessLabel: Label, e.g. who or what reads with it
settings.keepRecent: Latest messages kept as they are
settings.maxParallel: Agents working at the same time, per project
settings.maxParallelHint: How many members of one project work at once; a project can have its own number. An agent that only waits for a job does not count. 0 pauses the members; managers still answer.
settings.ownLoginNotice: Uses your own Claude account login. Whether this is allowed for third-party tools depends on Anthropic's terms for your plan; an API key is the officially supported option.
settings.sshKeyHint: Used for every repository with an SSH address (git@host:owner/repo.git) that has no key of its own. Add the public key to your account at the git host, or to a separate machine user. Works with GitHub, GitLab and any other host; agents can clone and push with it.
settings.sshKeyConfirmNew: Replace the SSH key? The old public key stops working here.
settings.sshKeyConfirmRemove: Remove the SSH key? Repositories that use it can no longer be reached.
settings.sshKeyOwn: Or use your own private key
settings.managerParallel: Managers may raise it up to
settings.managerParallelHint: A manager can change the number for its own project, up to this. 0: only people can change it.

archive.title: Archive
archive.hint: Done tickets move here {{days}} days after they were finished. Open one to restore it.
archive.hintManual: Archive done tickets with the button on the Done column. Open one to restore it.

secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.globalHint: Environment variables for all agents, e.g. tokens for CLI tools. Agents see the names and descriptions, never the values, which are hidden in chats and logs.
secrets.projectHint: Only for this project's agents. A secret with the same name as a global one replaces it here.
secrets.description: What it is for (agents see this)

skills.hint: A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md (name and description at its top) and what it needs. Upload it as a zip or as a single SKILL.md, or take it from a repository: the project's GitHub token opens a private one. PlainBoard puts it into each agent's folder before its next turn.
skills.notClaude: Only Claude agents that write code use skills; these don't: {{names}}.
skills.noAgents: No agent chosen: nobody gets it.

account.title: Your account
account.hint: Your picture, your name, your password and what you are told.
account.pictureHint: Shown with what you write in the chat. Without one, your initial stands there.
account.pictureUnreadable: This file is not a picture the browser can read.
account.showMentionsHint: Browser notifications while PlainBoard is open when someone mentions you. Off: no notifications; mentions are still recorded.

mcp.title: MCP / API access
mcp.description: Use PlainBoard from your own AI client: Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor and others.
mcp.intro: A personal token lets an MCP client (or a script against the API) work as you: it reads and changes exactly what you may in the browser, in your projects with your role. Create one per client, copy it now (it is shown once), and revoke it when the client no longer needs it.
mcp.enabledHint: For everyone on this PlainBoard. Off: the MCP server answers nothing and no personal token is accepted.
mcp.off: MCP and personal tokens are switched off on this PlainBoard.
mcp.label: Label, e.g. which client uses it
mcp.copy: Copy the token now: it is shown only this once. It is filled into the configurations below.
mcp.confirmRevoke: Revoke the token "{{name}}"? Clients that use it stop working at once.
mcp.clientsHint: The address of the MCP server is {{url}}. It takes the token as "Authorization: Bearer …"; the browser login does not count there.

users.title: People
users.hint: Who can sign in. Admins run the installation and see every project; everyone else sees the projects they were added to (project settings, Members). Changes apply at once.
users.addHint: Give them the user name and the password. They can change the password themselves.
users.pictureHint: Shown with what they write in the chat. Without one, their initial stands there.
users.usernameHint: They sign in with it. Browsers already signed in stay signed in.
users.limitsHint: What the projects this person creates may use, whoever works in them. Their projects only ever see these.
users.mayUseShared: May use the shared secrets and GitHub token
users.maxProjectsHint: How many projects of their own they may have. Empty: any number.
users.maxParallelHint: Across all their projects together, on top of each project's own number. Empty: no limit of their own.

members.rolesHint: Viewer: reads everything, changes nothing. Member: works with the board, the agents and the team. Owner: also these settings, repositories, secrets and members.
members.none: Nobody yet. Only admins see this project.
members.nobodyElse: Everyone with an account is a member. An admin adds further people under PlainBoard settings → People.
members.readOnly: You are a viewer of this project: you can read everything and change nothing.
members.readOnlyShort: You can view this project but not change it.
members.projectOwnerHint: Whose permissions apply to this project: subscriptions, runners, parallel limit and shared secrets.
members.makeOwnerIntro: From now on, what {{name}} may use applies to this project. {{name}} gets the role owner; the current project owner keeps the role owner.

change.nothing: Nothing else changes for this project.
change.runnerBlocked: {{name}} may not use this project's runner ({{runner}}). Move the project to a runner they may use first (Settings → Runner), then hand it over.
change.unpinned: Chosen subscription not allowed, will choose automatically: {{list}}. The project's manager is told.
change.losesShared: The installation's secrets, GitHub token and shared MCP servers are no longer available; the project's own stay.
change.parallel: Members working at once (across all projects of the owner): {{before}} → {{after}}

subscriptions.label: Subscriptions
subscriptions.title: Which AI subscriptions do the agents work with?
subscriptions.intro: Agents need at least one. Add every subscription or API key you want to use: with several, an agent takes the one that has the most room left, and a project can name its own.
subscriptions.advice: An API key is the officially supported way and is billed per token, which adds up with a busy team. A Claude subscription has a fixed price; whether it may be used here depends on Anthropic's terms for your plan. The connection is tested when you continue.
subscriptions.missing: Add one subscription or API key first.

models.label: Models
models.title: Which models do new agents get?
models.intro: These are the defaults for new projects and new agents. Every agent can be changed later, and so can these.
models.advice: Recommended: {{manager}} for managers, {{worker}} for members, {{summary}} for summaries.
models.managerHint: The manager plans, splits work and decides. A wrong decision costs the whole team time, so the strongest model pays off here.
models.workerHint: Members write the code. A balanced model does most of it well; the manager can give a hard piece of work more effort.
models.summaryHint: Compresses long chats and writes the state of a ticket. Routine work: the small model is enough and saves quota.
models.effortHint: Beside each model: how long it thinks before it acts. Higher is slower and uses more quota. The manager has many short turns, so medium is enough there; members and summaries start on high.

code.label: Code access
code.title: How do agents reach your repositories?
code.intro: Agents clone, push and open pull requests. Whatever you set here holds for every project; a project or a single repository can have its own access instead.
code.advice: Nothing here is required. With GitHub: a token (fine-grained, for the repositories: contents and pull requests read and write; actions and commit statuses read). With any other host: the SSH key, added to your account there. Public repositories that are only read need neither.
code.tokenHint: Not set. Leave it empty if you don't use GitHub.
code.authorHint: The name and address on the agents' commits.

pace.label: Pace
pace.title: How many agents work at the same time?
pace.intro: More agents finish sooner and use the subscription's quota faster. The number counts per project, and a project can have its own.
pace.advice: Recommended: start with 3. Raise it when the quota lasts through the week, lower it when it runs out early.
pace.timezoneHint: Taken from your browser. Schedules and the times agents see use it.

secrets.label: Secrets
secrets.title: Do the agents need keys or tokens of yours?
secrets.intro: Environment variables for the agents' shells, in every project: a package registry token, a deploy key, an API key of a service. Agents see the names, never the values in a chat. Skip this if nothing comes to mind; projects can have their own.

people.label: People
people.title: Does anyone else work here?
people.intro: Add the people you want to work with. They see nothing until you add them to a project, as a viewer, a member or an owner. Skip this to work alone; you can add people any time in the settings.

basics.label: Project
basics.title: What is the project called?
basics.intro: A project has its own board, its own team of agents, notes and schedules. What it is about you tell the manager in the chat afterwards: the first ticket on the board is for that.
basics.runnerHint: Its repositories are cloned there and its setup script runs there. Moving it later starts over on the other runner.
basics.runnerAway: This runner is not connected right now: the agents start once it is.

code.label: Code
code.title: Where is the code?
code.intro: Add the git repositories the agents work in. A project can also start without one, for planning or research.
code.advice: Per repository you decide how changes reach the base branch. Short, reliable checks: leave it as it is. Long or flaky check runs: switch on "land first", so branches merge at once and the base is checked afterwards.

team.label: Team
team.title: Who leads the work?
team.intro: Every project starts with a manager. You talk to it; it builds the team it needs, hands out the work and reports back.
team.advice: The defaults from the settings are filled in. Change them only if this project differs: a small side project runs fine on a smaller model and fewer agents.
team.subscriptionHint: Which subscription this project's agents run on. Useful when a project should use up its own quota; an agent can still be given another one.
team.providerHint: Whose models the manager runs on. The one from the PlainBoard settings is filled in; members can each run on another.
team.subscriptionAuto: Automatic: the one with the most room left

secrets.label: Secrets
secrets.title: Does this project need keys or tokens?
secrets.intro: Environment variables for the agents of this project only. One with the same name as a general secret wins here. Skip this if the project needs none.

members.label: People
members.title: Who works on this with you?
members.intro: You own this project. Add others as viewers, members or owners, or leave it as it is to work alone.
members.introAdmin: Admins see every project. Add others as viewers, members or owners, or leave it as it is to work alone.

settingsPage.atOnce: Changes here are stored at once.

own.label: My subscriptions
own.description: Your own subscriptions and API keys, for your projects and whom you share them with.
own.hint: Your projects run on these, besides what an admin allows you. Only you and admins can change or delete them; a token or key is never shown again. A sign-in in the browser (Claude login, ChatGPT) is kept for that subscription only and goes to the runner only while one of its turns runs, never into the runner's shared home.
own.peoplesHint: Added by people for their projects. You can change, share and delete them; their tokens and keys are not shown to you either.

subscriptions.label: Subscriptions
subscriptions.description: What the agents run on. Add every subscription or API key you want to use; with several, an agent takes the one with the most room left, and a project can name its own.

models.label: Models
models.description: What a new agent starts with. Every agent can be changed in its project's team; these only fill in the form.
models.providerHint: Which kind of agent a new agent is.
models.keepRecentHint: When a chat is summarised, this many of the latest messages stay as they are.

code.label: Code access
code.description: How agents reach your git repositories, in every project. A project or a single repository can have its own access instead.
code.tokenHint: Lets agents clone, push and open pull requests on GitHub. Leave it empty if you don't use GitHub.

pace.label: Pace
pace.description: How many agents work at the same time. More finish sooner and use the subscriptions faster.

general.description: Time zone, messages to members and updates.
general.timezoneHint: For schedules and for the times agents see.

projectSettings.title: Project settings
projectSettings.ownersOnly: Only owners of this project change its settings.

general.label: General
general.description: The project's name, and what its agents should know about it.

repositories.label: Repositories
repositories.description: The code the agents work in, and how their finished work reaches it. Click a repository to change its settings.
repositories.none: No repository yet. Without one, agents work in an empty folder.

team.label: Team
team.description: How this project's agents work together. Each agent's own model and instructions are in the Team view.

board.label: Board
board.description: What happens to tickets by themselves.

skills.label: Skills
skills.description: Claude skills for this project's agents: instructions and scripts they load when a task calls for them.

secrets.description: Keys and tokens for this project's agents only, as environment variables. Agents see the names, never the values. One with the same name as a general secret wins here.

members.label: Members
members.description: Who sees this project and what they may do. Admins always see it.

advanced.label: Advanced
advanced.description: Rarely needed. Leave these empty unless you know you need them.
advanced.deleteFiles: Also delete the folders its agents worked in
advanced.deletingNote: Deleting. With its folders this can take a few minutes; the window closes when it is done.
advanced.deleteFilesHint: Their clones of your repositories on this server, with everything in them that was never pushed. If they stay, a new project with the same name works in them again and finds the old state.
advanced.folderStays: The project works in your folder "{{folder}}". It stays as it is.
advanced.deleteHint: Deletes the board with all tickets, the team with its chats, the notes and the schedules. The code in your repositories stays. This cannot be undone.

previews.title: Previews
previews.confirmStop: Stop the server of "{{name}}"? Its preview ends for everyone. An agent can start it again.
previews.localOnly: Listens on 127.0.0.1 only, so it opens here and not in a tab.

runners.title: Runners
runners.description: Let a project's agents work on another server.
runners.intro: The agents of a project can work on a server of their own: more room, more power, or kept apart from the rest.
runners.requirements: The server needs Docker and internet access. No open port or domain needed.
runners.step1Done: "{{name}}" is added. Now set it up on the server.
runners.stepFile: On that server, make an empty folder and save this as docker-compose.yml in it
runners.stepRun: On that server, run this command
runners.onceNote: This contains the access key for the server. It is shown only now: copy it before you leave this page.
runners.stepWait: Wait until it shows as connected
runners.waiting: Waiting for the server to connect…
runners.stepChooseHint: Open the project's settings, section Runner, and choose this server.
runners.updateHint: The runner updates itself to PlainBoard's version when nothing runs on it. Should that ever fail, PlainBoard says so; then run this in the same folder:
runners.offlineHint: Is the container running on that server? Check with
runners.versionMismatch: It runs another version than PlainBoard and updates itself when nothing runs on it. If it stays like this: in the runner's folder run docker compose pull && docker compose up -d.
runners.updating: Updating… new turns and jobs wait until it is back
runners.restartsIn: restarts at the latest in {{minutes}} min
runners.keyConfirm: Create a new access key for "{{name}}"? The old one stops working at once: start the runner again with the new command.
runners.removeConfirm: Remove "{{name}}"? Its server keeps its files; stop the container there.

projectRunner.title: Runner
projectRunner.description: Where this project's agents work: on this server or on another one.
projectRunner.label: Where the agents work
projectRunner.hint: More servers are added in Settings > Runners.
projectRunner.hintNone: To use another server, add it first in Settings > Runners.
projectRunner.busy: Not possible right now: agents of this project are working. Pause the project or wait until they are done.
projectRunner.confirmBody: The agents start fresh on the new server and clone the repositories again. Nothing is lost here: the files stay where they are.
projectRunner.unpushedChecking: Looking for work that is not pushed yet…
projectRunner.unpushedNone: Every workspace on "{{runner}}" is pushed: nothing stays behind.
projectRunner.unpushedTitle: Not pushed yet: this stays behind on "{{runner}}"
projectRunner.unpushedUnchecked: "{{runner}}" could not be checked for work that is not pushed yet: {{detail}}
projectRunner.sessionsReset: Each agent starts a new session there; tools they installed must be installed again.

pause.title: Pause everything
pause.description: Brings every project to rest, for an update or a restart of the server. Agents finish their current step and save their work, and PlainBoard stops their background jobs and preview servers. Nothing is lost: everything goes on where it stopped when you resume, and agents start again what they still need.
pause.step1: Pause everything. Agents that are working are told to wrap up; nothing new starts.
pause.step2: Wait until this page says that everything is at rest. That usually takes a few minutes.
pause.step3: Update or restart PlainBoard. The pause holds across the restart.
pause.resumeHint: The agents that were paused work on with what they had open, and what waited meanwhile starts.
pause.standingHint: You can update or restart PlainBoard now: docker compose pull, then docker compose up -d. Afterwards, resume here.
pause.servers_one: {{count}} server of a preview still runs. It is stopped as soon as its agent has finished its step.
pause.servers_other: {{count}} servers of previews still run. They are stopped as soon as their agents have finished their step.
pause.bannerMoving_one: PlainBoard is being paused by {{by}}: {{count}} thing is still wrapping up.
pause.bannerMoving_other: PlainBoard is being paused by {{by}}: {{count}} things are still wrapping up.
pause.bannerStanding: PlainBoard is paused by {{by}}. Everything is at rest; nothing starts until it is resumed.

move.label: Move the project
move.description: The whole project as one file: its settings, the team with its notes and task lists, the board with its history, notes, schedules and repositories. On the other PlainBoard, choose New project and bring the file along. The code is not in the file: it comes from git again, so everything the agents built should be pushed first.
move.passphraseHint: Optional. With one, the file also carries the credentials (GitHub tokens, SSH keys, secrets, the environment of MCP servers), sealed with it. Without one they stay here and are entered again on the other side.
move.passphraseOwnerOnly: Only the project's owner or an admin can take the credentials along: the file is made without them.
move.passphraseImportHint: The one the file was made with. Leave it empty if there was none.
move.chatsHint: The conversations with every agent. Without them the agents start with empty chats, but keep their notes and task lists.
move.exportNote: Best when the project is at rest (PlainBoard settings, Pause everything): work that is still open is closed on the other side and ordered again from there. This project stays as it is.
move.importTitle: Or bring a project from another PlainBoard
move.fileHint: The .plainboard.zip that the other PlainBoard made under Project settings, Move the project.
move.missing: Not in the file, enter these again:
move.importedNote: You are its owner. Nothing has started: check the subscription and the repositories' access under Project settings, then tell the manager to go on.

usage.title: Usage
usage.description: How much disk, memory and CPU PlainBoard uses: per volume, per project and agent, and what all agents share. Folder sizes are measured in the background every few hours, the CPU every half minute.
usage.cpuNone: No CPU measured yet. It appears after a minute.
usage.cpuHint: Percent of the whole machine ({{cores}} cores); 100 % is every core busy. Per project the CPU of its agents' turns, jobs and preview servers and of landing checks; the chart stacks its agents over the last 24 hours, all on the same scale. The line is the host's load average.
usage.runnerDown: The runner cannot be reached: only the app's own volumes are shown.
usage.runnerNothingKnown: Nothing is known of it yet.
usage.low: Little room left. Free some space before agents stop because the disk is full.
usage.projectsHint: An agent's disk is its own workspace; its memory is what runs in it now: its turn, jobs and preview servers. "Other" is a folder all agents of the project share, folders of former agents and the clones its branches land in.
usage.otherMemory: Memory of the runner itself and its browsers
usage.sharedHint: The agents' home: toolchains, caches and sign-ins. It serves every agent, so it is not counted for one.
usage.agentFigures: Disk of its workspace · memory of what runs in it now

cleanup.title: Disk space
cleanup.notifyHint: The disk should stay below this. From here on, or earlier when the trend crosses it within two hours, the manager of the project causing it hears it and cleans up with his tools. Nothing is deleted without him.
cleanup.emergencyHint: Only this near full PlainBoard deletes by itself: old job logs, cache files unused for a month, folders of removed agents without unpushed work, build outputs of members idle for a day. Above the target it only trims big shared tool caches (sccache, cargo, npm, pip), oldest entries first. The managers hear exactly what.
cleanup.auto: Emergency cleanup and stopping idle servers
cleanup.hint: Never touched by itself: folders of members who work or have an open assignment, unpushed work, uploads, the database, secrets.
cleanup.memory: Stop idle servers below (% memory free)
cleanup.memoryHint: Preview servers of idle agents that nobody opened for 12 hours.
cleanup.toolDetailsHint: After this, tool steps in chats keep only a short preview of input and result; chat texts, tickets, comments and reports always stay complete. 0: forever (the value after an update, so nothing goes unasked).

notice.soon: {{when}}: {{percent}} % used, the target was near. Told: {{projects}}.

summary.emergency: {{when}}: near full, PlainBoard deleted {{freed}} by itself ({{free}} were free).
summary.trim: {{when}}: above the target, PlainBoard trimmed shared tool caches by {{freed}} ({{free}} were free).

search.title: Semantic search
search.description: Agents find the projects' history by meaning: earlier tickets, reports, decisions, notes and commits.
search.hint: Indexes tickets, reports, decisions, comments, notes and commits in the background and gives the agents a search tool. The embedding model runs on this server (no key, no cost) and is downloaded once. Each project can switch it off for itself.
search.unavailable: Semantic search needs PostgreSQL with the extension pgvector (e.g. the image pgvector/pgvector). With SQLite, or a server without it, it is not available.

modelState.absent: not downloaded yet (when there is something to index)

search.rebuilt: {{done}} of {{total}} chunks embedded; search uses the current model until all are
search.modelsHint: All run on this server's CPU, need no key and understand German and English in one space. A larger model finds better, but indexes more slowly and needs more memory. Quality: MMTEB multilingual retrieval score (higher is better).
search.facts: {{tier}} · {{dim}} dimensions · up to {{tokens}} tokens · {{download}} MB download · about {{ram}} MB memory · {{licence}}
search.confirmText: Every chunk is embedded again with the new model: {{count}} chunks, which takes {{duration}} on this server (plus a download of {{download}} MB). Meanwhile search keeps using {{current}}; when the new index is complete it switches at once and the old vectors are deleted.
search.confirmBack: Stay with the current model: the new index for {{model}} is called off and what it has so far is deleted.

customerLanguages.hint: Every change is saved at once. Removing a language keeps its texts on the tickets: they come back when you add it again.
customerLanguages.confirmRemove: {{count}} tickets have customer texts in {{language}}. Remove the language anyway? The texts stay stored and come back when you add {{language}} again.
